question: What is a push token, and why does a user end up with several of them?
answer_hinglish:
Push token ek device-specific address hai. Jab app phone par install hoti hai, OS ka push service (Android par FCM, iOS par APNs) us install ko ek token deta hai, aur app woh token hamare backend ko bhej deti hai. Push bhejne ke liye hum provider ko bolte hain "is token par yeh message" -- token hi address hai, jaise email ke liye email address.

Ek user ke paas kai tokens kyun? Kyunki ek token ek INSTALL ka hai, user ka nahi. Phone aur tablet dono par app hai toh do tokens. Naya phone liya aur purana unregister nahi kiya toh purana token bhi pada rehta hai. App reinstall ki toh naya token mil jaata hai. Stage 1 mein `Recipient` mein ek hi `pushToken` tha; stage 3 mein yeh `pushTokens: string[]` ban gaya.

Isse teen sawal khade hote hain jo is project ne solve kiye: (1) ek push notification sab devices tak kaise jaaye -- ek delivery, send time par fan-out; (2) dead tokens ka kya karein -- provider `invalidAddress` bole toh token user se hata do; (3) stale tokens jama na hon -- 10 tokens ka cap, sabse purana drop. Interview mein main bolunga: "token device ka address hai, aur devices aate jaate rehte hain, isliye address list ko manage karna padta hai".
why_needed: Bina multi-device support ke sirf ek device (aksar sabse purana ya sabse naya) ko push milta, aur tablet par notification kabhi nahi aata.
real_world_analogy: Ek ghar ke do letterbox -- ek front door par, ek back door par. Postman ko dono ka pata chahiye, aur jo letterbox tod diya gaya uska pata list se kaatna padta hai.
how_it_works: App start par token register karti hai (`POST /users/:id/push-tokens`), logout par hata deti hai (`DELETE`). Send ke time worker user ke current tokens padhta hai aur har token ke liye ek provider call karta hai.
in_this_project: `src/types.ts` mein `Recipient.pushTokens?: string[]` (comment: one per device). `addressesFor(recipient, "push")` saare non-blank, de-duplicated tokens deta hai. `src/users.ts` mein `PushTokenRegistry` interface (`addPushToken`, `removePushToken`) aur `InMemoryUsers` uska in-memory version. Tests: `test/devices.test.ts` ka `THREE` user teen tokens ke saath.
advantages: Har device tak notification pahunchta hai
Address list ek jagah (UserDirectory) mein manage hoti hai
Email / SMS ka path bilkul same rehta hai
disadvantages: Tokens stale ho jaate hain, unhe hatane ka mechanism chahiye
Har device ek alag provider call hai (cost aur load)
common_mistakes: Token ko user ka permanent id samajhna
Ek hi pushToken field rakhna aur naya token purane ko overwrite kar de
Logout par token unregister na karna

question: Why is a push to several devices one delivery with a per-device log, and not one delivery per device?
answer_hinglish:
Seedha jawab: kyunki "first" mode ka matlab hai "pehla CHANNEL jo user tak pahunche", aur phone plus tablet do channels nahi, ek channel hain. Agar har device ki alag delivery hoti, toh OTP (push, else SMS, else email) ka logic toot jaata -- kya tablet fail hone par SMS bhejein jabki phone par push pahunch gaya? Delivery-per-device mein "user tak pahuncha ya nahi" ka sawal hi bikhar jaata.

Isliye design: ek push delivery, aur uske andar `devices: DeviceResult[]` -- har token ka last answer (`sent` + providerId, ya `failed` + error + retryable, aur `removed` agar token dead tha). Delivery ka result in answers ko fold karke banta hai: koi ek device accept kare toh delivery `sent`, kyunki user reach ho gaya.

Faayde: record ka shape same rehta hai (ek channel = ek delivery), status calculation (`notificationStatus`) nahi badla, `maxAttempts` ab bhi rounds ka matlab rakhta hai, aur email / SMS / single-device push bilkul purane path par chalte hain -- README kehta hai stage 1 aur 2 mein sirf push key wale 3 tests aur randomized checks update hue.

Kya chhoda: per-device status ki first-class query nahi hai (log sirf "last answer" hai), aur per-device preferences (tablet mute karo) built nahi hain. Main interview mein yeh trade-off openly bolunga: model user-centric hai, device-centric nahi.
why_needed: Delivery ka model tay karta hai ki modes, retries aur status kaise kaam karenge; galat granularity choose ki toh 'first' mode ka matlab hi badal jaata.
real_world_analogy: Courier ek parcel ek ghar ko deta hai, chahe ghar mein do darwaze hon. Courier ki diary mein likha hota hai kis darwaze par try kiya, par parcel ek hi hai.
how_it_works: Delivery planning ek push delivery banata hai. Send time par `sendToAddresses` har token ko call karta hai aur answers ko ek result mein fold karta hai, plus `deviceLog` har token ka entry update karta hai.
in_this_project: PLAN.md stage 3 decision: "Several push devices: one delivery, fanned out at send time, with a per-device log. Recommended over one delivery per device: first mode means the first channel that reaches the user". `src/record.ts` mein `Delivery.devices?: DeviceResult[]` aur `DeviceResult { token, status, providerId?, error?, retryable?, removed? }`. Test: 'one push delivery, one round, a call per device with its own provider key; all logged'.
advantages: 'first' mode ka matlab safe rehta hai
Record aur status logic unchanged
Har device ka last answer debugging ke liye dikhta hai
disadvantages: Per-device history nahi, sirf last answer
Per-device preferences ka natural jagah nahi hai
common_mistakes: Device ko channel samajh lena
Per-device delivery banakar 'first' mode mein SMS bhi bhej dena
Device log ko delivery ka status samajhna

question: Walk through sendToAddresses: how are the answers of several device calls folded into one delivery result?
answer_hinglish:
`sendToAddresses` (src/planner.ts) delivery ke saare CURRENT addresses par parallel calls karta hai -- email / SMS ke liye ek, push ke liye har device ka ek -- aur answers ko ek `CallResult` mein fold karta hai. Rules order mein:

1. Sirf ek answer hai toh woh as is pass through -- email, SMS aur single-device push bilkul pehle jaise behave karte hain.
2. Koi bhi device `sent` -> poori delivery `sent`. User reach ho gaya; jo devices is round mein fail hue unhe retry nahi karte.
3. Har call open circuit ne refuse ki (`called === false`) -> `"circuit-open"`, taaki notifier stage 2 ka circuit-open path le ("first" fail over, "all" wait).
4. Warna koi failure retryable hai (ya kisi ek ko circuit ne refuse kiya) -> retryable failure.
5. Warna permanent failure, reason mein har token ka kaaran: `no device accepted (tok-a: x; tok-b: y)`.

Saath mein do aur cheezein return hoti hain: `called` (koi asli provider call hui ya nahi -- isi se attempts badhte hain) aur `sentIds` (har accepting device ka providerId, taaki receipt kisi bhi device ki aaye, delivery ki maani jaaye). Aur `devices` log -- par function delivery ko KHUD change nahi karta. Comment saaf kehta hai: caller likhega, queued notifier sirf lease check ke baad. Yeh separation hi stalled-worker bug ko rokta hai.

Ek subtle point: mixed case (ek device circuit-open, doosra permanent) retryable maana jaata hai, kyunki circuit wala device abhi try hi nahi hua.
why_needed: Kai answers ko ek decision mein badalna hi multi-device ka core hai; yeh rule galat hua toh ya toh OTP late hoga ya user ko duplicate aayega.
real_world_analogy: Exam result: kisi bhi ek paper mein pass hona kaafi hai (sent); sab mein fail aur re-exam allowed ho toh re-exam (retryable); sab mein permanently disqualified toh final fail.
how_it_works: `Promise.all(targets.map(call))`, phir `answers.find(sent)`, `answers.some(a => a !== 'circuit-open')`, `answers.some(retryable)` -- teen checks priority order mein.
in_this_project: `src/planner.ts::sendToAddresses` dono notifiers share karte hain: `src/queued-notifier.ts` apna `call` deta hai (breaker + timeout + `BrokenCircuitError` -> `"circuit-open"`), `src/notifier.ts` stage 1 seedha `sendOnce`. Tests: 'one device accepted, one dead: sent', 'every device failed for good: a permanent failure, and first moves to the next channel' (error string exactly `no device accepted (tok-a: x; tok-b: y)`), 'every device's call refused by an open circuit'.
advantages: Ek jagah ka rule, dono notifiers mein same
Single address ka path unchanged (regression risk kam)
Delivery ko mutate nahi karta -- lease check caller ke haath
disadvantages: Ek slow device poore round ko slow karta hai (Promise.all sabka wait)
Sirf 'last answer' log, history nahi
common_mistakes: Sab devices fail hone tak wait karke ek success ignore karna
Circuit-open ko normal retryable failure maan lena (D6)
Function ke andar hi delivery mutate kar dena
follow_up_questions: Why is a mix of circuit-open and permanent failure retryable?
What does `called` control?
Why does a slow device delay the whole round, and how would you fix it?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Parallel calls (`Promise.all`) latency ko sabse slow device tak le jaate hain, par har call ka apna timeout hai (stage 2 TimeoutPolicy), toh worst case bounded hai. Fold rule user-centric hai: 'kisi ek ne accept kiya' kaafi maana. Alternative 'sab devices tak pahuncho' strict hota par ek dead tablet ke liye poori delivery retry hoti.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Ek device ki call hang ho toh timeout usse retryable failure banata hai. Agar sab calls circuit ne refuse ki aur rule galat hota (D6) toh OTP wait karta, SMS par nahi jaata. Lease khone wala worker fold kar leta hai par likh nahi paata -- isliye fold aur write alag hain.
advanced.alternatives: Provider ka multicast API (FCM ek request mein kai tokens) -- README mein not built. `Promise.allSettled` bhi chal sakta tha, par `call` khud kabhi reject nahi karta, isliye `all` kaafi hai.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x devices per user nahi honge (cap 10), par 100x users par provider calls devices ke multiple mein badhti hain; tab multicast aur per-provider rate limit zaroori hote hain.
advanced.production_improvements: Per-device latency metrics, multicast batching, aur ek slow device ko round se alag karna (jo pehle accept kare uske baad baaki ko background mein chhodna) -- yeh sab production additions hain, yahan built nahi.

question: Why are the push targets read when the job runs (fan-out at send time) instead of when the notification is created?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki job aur request ke beech time ka gap ho sakta hai -- retry backoff, quiet hours ka deferral, queue ka backlog -- aur us beech user ki device list badal sakti hai. Agar targets `notify()` ke time freeze kar dete, toh do galtiyan hoti: naya device (jo user ne abhi login kiya) retry miss kar deta, aur ek token jo beech mein dead declare hua uspar bhi bhejte rehte.

Isliye `pushTargets()` user ke tokens JOB RUN hone ke time `deps.users.get()` se padhta hai, aur unme se woh hata deta hai jo isi delivery ke pichhle attempt par permanently fail hue the. Yeh wahi lesson hai jo stage 1 ne sikhaya tha: deferred delivery send time par dobara plan hoti hai (`replan`), kyunki "plan time ka sach" send time tak purana ho jaata hai.

Ek safety net bhi hai: agar is filtering ke baad koi token nahi bachta, toh `[delivery.to!]` use hota hai -- planner ne abhi ek address dekha tha, "never send to nobody". Aur agar user ke saare tokens hi chale gaye, toh `replan` delivery ko `skipped (no_address)` kar deta hai.

Test 'a device registered between two attempts gets the retry': pehla round tok-1 par 503, phir `users.addPushToken("u1", "tok-new")`, retry mein calls `tok-1, tok-1, tok-new` aur delivery sent.
why_needed: Queued system mein request aur send ke beech minutes ya ghante lag sakte hain; us waqt ka data hi sahi data hai.
real_world_analogy: Party ka invitation bhejne se pehle guest list dobara check karna -- hafte bhar mein kisi ne naya number diya ho ya kisi ka number band ho gaya ho.
how_it_works: Job run -> `replan` (address hai ya nahi) -> `pushTargets` (current tokens minus is delivery ke dead tokens) -> har target ki call.
in_this_project: `src/planner.ts::pushTargets`: `addressesFor(recipient, "push").filter((t) => !dead.has(t))`, jahan `dead` = `delivery.devices` ke woh entries jinka `status === "failed" && retryable === false`. PLAN.md: "The tokens are read when the job RUNS (a device registered between two attempts gets the retry)".
advantages: Naye devices retry mein shamil
Removed tokens par dobara call nahi
Stage 1 ke replan lesson ke saath consistent
disadvantages: Har attempt par user lookup (real system mein ek service / DB call)
Attempts ke beech target list badalti hai, toh 'kis par bheja' sirf device log se pata chalta hai
common_mistakes: Job payload mein tokens copy kar dena
Dead tokens ko filter na karna aur har retry par unhe call karna
Khaali target list par chup chaap 'sent' maan lena
follow_up_questions: What if the user unregisters every device between two attempts?
Why fall back to delivery.to instead of an empty list?
How does the provider idempotency key stay stable when targets change?

question: Why does each device get its own provider idempotency key <id>:push:<token> instead of one key per delivery?
answer_hinglish:
Queue at-least-once hai: lease khone wala worker bhej chuka ho sakta hai aur naya owner dobara bhejega. Isliye har send ke saath ek provider idempotency key jaati hai jo har attempt par SAME hoti hai, taaki key support karne wala provider duplicate drop kar de. Stage 2 mein yeh `<notificationId>:<channel>` thi.

Multi-device ke saath yeh key toot jaati. Socho key `n1:push` rahe aur ek delivery do devices ko jaaye: provider ke liye tok-a ka message aur tok-b ka message dono `n1:push` hain -- doosre ko woh pehle ka duplicate samajh ke DROP kar dega. Matlab tablet ko kabhi notification nahi milega. Isliye key ab device ke saath hai: `${record.id}:push:${to}`.

Yeh key do cheezon par stable hai: (1) retry par -- same token, same key, toh duplicate safe; (2) device list badalne par -- tok-new aaya toh uski apni nayi key, tok-a ki key nahi badli. Agar key mein device ka index (`:push:0`) hota toh list badalte hi keys shift ho jaatin aur wrong dedupe hota.

Honest note: fakes dedupe nahi karte; tests key ko check karte hain, provider behaviour ko nahi. Test: `push.attempts.map(m => [m.to, m.idempotencyKey])` == `[["tok-a", "n1:push:tok-a"], ...]`. README: push key ka change sirf 3 tests aur randomized checks update karke hua.
why_needed: At-least-once delivery mein duplicates ko rokne ka ek hi tareeka hai -- receiver ko stable key dena. Key ki granularity galat hui toh ya duplicates aate hain ya asli messages drop hote hain.
real_world_analogy: Courier ka tracking number har parcel ka alag hota hai. Agar do alag gharon ke parcels ka ek hi number ho, toh system doosre ko 'already delivered' samajh lega.
how_it_works: `outboundMessage(record, delivery, to)` key banata hai: push ke liye `<id>:push:<to>`, baaki channels ke liye `<id>:<channel>`. Har call apna message banati hai.
in_this_project: `src/planner.ts::outboundMessage` mein `idempotencyKey: delivery.channel === "push" ? `${record.id}:push:${to}` : `${record.id}:${delivery.channel}``. `src/types.ts` ke `OutboundMessage.idempotencyKey` comment mein bhi documented. Stage 2 mutation S25 ('provider key changes per attempt') pakda gaya tha.
advantages: Retry par duplicate-safe
Device list badalne par bhi stable
Doosre device ka message galti se drop nahi hota
disadvantages: Token key ka hissa hai -- token lamba ho sakta hai (4096 tak), kuch providers key length limit karte hain
Fakes dedupe nahi karte, toh asli guarantee provider par nirbhar
common_mistakes: Per-delivery key multi-device par reuse karna
Key mein list index ya attempt number daalna
Maan lena ki idempotency key exactly-once deti hai
follow_up_questions: What breaks if the key contains the attempt number?
How would you shorten the key if a provider limits its length?
Does the key make delivery exactly-once? Why not?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Key ki granularity = dedupe ki granularity. Per-device key se har device independent dedupe hota hai. Trade-off: key lamba ho sakta hai; production mein `hash(token)` use karke fixed length kar sakte hain, stability same rehti hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar provider key support na kare (ya TTL ke baad bhool jaaye) toh stalled worker aur naya owner dono bhej denge -- user ko do push. Yeh documented at-least-once cost hai. Key mein index hota toh device remove hone par galat device dedupe hota.
advanced.alternatives: Provider-side dedupe ki jagah apni side par 'sent' marker (outbox table) -- par provider call aur DB write ek transaction mein nahi aa sakte, toh window fir bhi rehti hai.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 100x traffic par provider ki dedupe window aur key storage unka concern hai; hamara kaam sirf stable key bhejna hai. Multicast API par per-token key ka support provider-specific hota hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Key ka hashed fixed-length form, provider ke dedupe window ka documentation check karna, aur metrics: same key ke kitne repeat sends hue (lease loss ka signal).

question: When no device accepted, how does the retry go only to the devices that did not fail for good?
answer_hinglish:
Retry ek naya round hai, aur `pushTargets()` us round ke targets banata hai: user ke current tokens MINUS woh tokens jinka isi delivery ke device log mein `status: "failed"` aur `retryable: false` hai. Matlab jis device ne permanent "no" bola (bad token, unregistered), usse dobara call nahi hoti; jisne 503 ya timeout diya, woh retry mein shamil hai.

Device log ek Map ki tarah update hota hai (`deviceLog`): pichhli entries rehti hain, is round ke targets ki entries overwrite hoti hain. Isliye ek permanently failed token ki entry log mein bani rehti hai aur agle rounds use filter karte rehte hain, chahe woh token user ki list mein abhi bhi ho (`invalidAddress` na mila ho toh token hataya nahi jaata).

Test 'nobody accepted, one retryable': tok-a `failed(false, "bad token")`, tok-b `failed(true, "503")`. Delivery `pending, attempts 1`. Clock 1 s aage, drain: calls `tok-a, tok-b, tok-b` -- teesri call sirf tok-b ko. Final: `sent, attempts 2`, log `tok-a:failed, tok-b:sent`.

Kab poori delivery fail hoti hai? Jab is round mein koi retryable failure nahi bachi (sab permanent) -- tab `failed` aur "first" mode agle channel par jaata hai. Aur agar retryable hai par `attempts` `maxAttempts` tak pahunch gaye, tab bhi failed.
why_needed: Permanent failure ko retry karna provider ko bekaar load deta hai aur breaker ke stats bigaadta nahi par time aur cost barbaad karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Doctor ke follow-up mein sirf woh tests dobara hote hain jo inconclusive the; jo clearly negative aaye unhe repeat nahi karte.
how_it_works: Round N ka log -> round N+1 ke `pushTargets` mein dead set -> sirf baaki tokens ki calls -> log merge.
in_this_project: `src/planner.ts::pushTargets` (dead set filter) aur `src/planner.ts::deviceLog` (Map merge: `new Map((delivery.devices ?? []).map((d) => [d.token, d]))`). Queued notifier mein retry `retryLater(job, delivery, now + backoff.delayMs(attempts))` se delayed job banta hai.
advantages: Permanent failures par koi wasted call nahi
Log merge se history ek round se agle tak chalti hai
Retry ke beech aaya naya device bhi shamil
disadvantages: Log sirf last answer rakhta hai, toh ek token ki purani retryable history nahi dikhti
Dead filter delivery-scoped hai; agli notification phir se us token ko try karegi agar woh hataya nahi gaya
common_mistakes: Retry mein saare tokens dobara call karna
Log ko har round replace karna (dead entries kho jaati)
Permanent failure ko token removal samajhna (sirf invalidAddress par hatate hain)

question: With several devices, what does one attempt mean, and why are attempts counted as rounds and not as provider calls?
answer_hinglish:
Is project mein ek attempt = ek ROUND of provider calls. Do devices ke saath ek round mein do calls hoti hain, par `delivery.attempts` sirf 1 badhta hai. Test isko exactly pin karta hai: 2 devices x 3 rounds = 6 provider calls, aur delivery `failed, attempts 3`.

Kyun? `maxAttempts` (default 3) ka matlab "kitni baar try karein" hai, aur backoff (`exponentialBackoff`) bhi attempt number se delay nikalta hai. Agar calls count hotin, toh teen devices wale user ka pehla hi round 3 attempts kha jaata aur koi retry hi nahi hota -- jitne zyada devices, utne kam retries. Yeh ulta hai: zyada devices wala user kam reliable ho jaata.

Ek aur rule: attempt tabhi count hota hai jab koi asli call hui. `if (called) delivery.attempts += 1` -- agar har call circuit breaker ne refuse ki (koi provider call nahi hui), toh attempt use nahi hota. Yeh stage 2 ka principle hai: "all" mode circuit open par wait karta hai bina attempt jalaaye, warna bina ek bhi asli try ke delivery fail ho jaati.

`Delivery.attempts` ka comment bhi yahi kehta hai: "provider calls made (a call refused by an open circuit is not one)" -- aur stage 3 ke baad uska matlab rounds hai.
why_needed: Retry budget aur backoff dono attempt number par chalte hain; unit galat hua toh multi-device users ke retries chupke se kam ho jaate.
real_world_analogy: Ek exam attempt mein teen papers hote hain -- teen papers dene se teen attempts nahi ho jaate.
how_it_works: Round chala -> `called` true hai toh `attempts++` -> result retryable aur `attempts < maxAttempts` toh backoff ke saath reschedule, warna failed.
in_this_project: `src/queued-notifier.ts`: `const { result, called, sentIds, devices } = await sendToAddresses(...)` ke baad `if (called) delivery.attempts += 1; // one attempt = one round of provider calls`. Test 'attempts count rounds, not calls: 2 devices x 3 rounds = 6 calls, 3 attempts, then failed'.
advantages: maxAttempts ka matlab devices ki ginti se independent
Backoff predictable
Circuit refusals retry budget nahi khaate
disadvantages: Provider calls ka total sirf provider.attempts / logs se dikhta hai, attempts field se nahi
common_mistakes: Har provider call par attempts++ karna
Circuit-open par bhi attempt count karna
Attempts ko provider cost ka measure samajhna

How is the backoff delay computed from the attempt number?

question: A dead token is removed at once even by a worker that lost its lease, but the device log is written only after the lease check. Why the asymmetry?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki dono writes alag cheezon ke baare mein hain, aur "kaun likh sakta hai" ka rule unki ownership se aata hai.

Device log DELIVERY ka state hai, aur delivery ka owner woh worker hai jiske paas job ki current lease hai. Stalled worker (jo provider par atka raha aur lease expire ho gayi) agar apna log likh de, toh woh naye owner ka result overwrite kar sakta hai -- bilkul stage 2 ka S22 bug, jahan stalled worker ne `pending` likh diya tha ek delivery par jo naya owner SENT kar chuka tha. Isliye `sendToAddresses` delivery ko mutate nahi karta, sirf `devices` return karta hai, aur queued notifier `if (!this.queue.owns(job.id, job.leaseToken, now)) return this.lostLease(); if (devices) delivery.devices = devices;` -- pehle lease, phir write.

Dead token removal USER ka fact hai, job ka nahi. Provider ne bola "yeh token UNREGISTERED hai" -- yeh baat sach hai chahe job kisi ke bhi paas ho. Agar lease na hone par ise bhi drop kar dete, toh woh dead token user ki list mein reh jaata aur har agli notification uspar bekaar call karti. Removal idempotent bhi hai (`removePushToken` doosri baar `false` deta hai), toh do workers dono hata dein toh bhi koi nuksaan nahi.

Test 'a worker that lost its lease does not write its device log over the new owner's': stalled worker ke `late` answers ke baad bhi log `["sent", "sent"]` rehta hai aur `stats.leaseLost >= 1`.
why_needed: Distributed workers mein har write ke liye sochna padta hai: yeh kiska state hai aur kya stale writer ise kharab kar sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Retire hua security guard (shift khatam) register mein entry nahi likh sakta, par agar usne dekha ki gate ka taala toota hai toh woh maintenance ko bata sakta hai -- taala toota hai, chahe duty par koi bhi ho.
how_it_works: `deviceLog()` ke andar hi `invalidAddress && !retryable` par `deps.users.removePushToken(...)` chalta hai (lease check se pehle). Log return hota hai; caller lease check ke baad assign karta hai.
in_this_project: `src/planner.ts::deviceLog`: `if (a.invalidAddress === true && !a.retryable && deps.users.removePushToken?.(record.userId, token)) entry.removed = true;`. `src/queued-notifier.ts`: `sendToAddresses` ke baad `now = this.clock.now(); if (!this.queue.owns(...)) return this.lostLease(); if (devices) delivery.devices = devices;`. `src/queue.ts::owns` token aur `leaseUntil > now` dono check karta hai.
advantages: Stale writer delivery state kharab nahi kar sakta
Dead token jaldi hatta hai, bekaar calls bachti hain
Removal idempotent hai, double removal safe
disadvantages: Do write paths ke alag rules -- naye developer ke liye samajhna mushkil
Lease khone wale worker ka `removed: true` log mein nahi dikhta (sirf user ki list badalti hai)
common_mistakes: Lease check ke bina koi bhi write karna
User-level facts ko bhi lease ke peeche rokna aur dead token chhod dena
Lease check send se PEHLE karke maan lena ki baad mein bhi lease hai

Is removing the token idempotent? What if two workers both remove it?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Lease token ek fencing token ki tarah hai: write sirf current owner kare. Par har write ko fence karna zaroori nahi -- jo fact job-independent aur idempotent hai (token dead), woh bina fence ke safe hai. Trade-off: do write rules, zyada sochna.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar removal bhi lease ke peeche hota: stalled worker ka dead answer kho jaata, token list mein rehta, agli notification phir call karti (provider phir bolta dead) -- self-healing par wasteful. Agar log fence na hota: naye owner ka 'sent' log purane 'late' failure se overwrite (test isi ko pakadta hai).
advanced.alternatives: Database mein: delivery row par `lease_token` / `version` column aur `UPDATE ... WHERE lease_token = $x`; token removal ek alag `DELETE FROM push_tokens WHERE user_id = $1 AND token = $2` jo idempotent hai.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bahut workers aur lambi provider latency par lease loss zyada hoga; tab `stats.leaseLost` metric important ho jaata hai aur leaseMs ko sendTimeoutMs se kaafi upar rakhna padta hai (constructor yeh enforce karta hai).
advanced.production_improvements: leaseLost ka alert, token removals ka audit log (kis provider response par hataya), aur removal ko user-service ke event (TokenInvalidated) ke roop mein publish karna.

question: What was gap D6, where every device was refused by an open circuit, and why did it matter for an OTP?
answer_hinglish:
D6 ek mutation check tha jo pehli run mein SURVIVE kar gaya -- matlab code toot gaya par koi test fail nahi hua. Mutation: "every device refused by an open circuit treated as an ordinary retryable failure".

Asal rule: agar ek round ki HAR call circuit breaker ne refuse ki (koi provider call hui hi nahi), toh `sendToAddresses` `"circuit-open"` return karta hai, aur notifier stage 2 ka circuit-open path leta hai: "first" mode turant agle channel par fail over karta hai, "all" mode bina attempt jalaaye breaker ke probe tak wait karta hai. Mutation ke saath yeh case normal retryable failure ban jaata: OTP ka push delivery backoff ke saath retry ke liye queue mein wait karta, jabki SMS turant bhej sakte the. User login screen par code ka wait karta rehta -- "first" mode ka poora point hi yahi hai ki dead channel ke around route karein.

Survive kyun hua? Single-device tests ne breaker khola tha, par kisi multi-device test ne nahi -- aur single-device path `answers.length === 1` par answer seedha pass kar deta hai, toh fold logic kabhi test nahi hua. Fix: naya test 'every device's call refused by an open circuit: first fails over to SMS at once, no attempt used' -- do failing calls se push breaker khulta hai, phir OTP: push `failed, error "circuit open", attempts 0`, SMS sent, aur `push.attempts` 2 hi rehta hai.
why_needed: Fail-over tabhi kaam karta hai jab system pehchaane ki channel 'down' hai, sirf 'flaky' nahi. Galat classification se time-critical message late hota hai.
real_world_analogy: Highway band hai (police ne rok diya) toh GPS turant doosra raasta deta hai; traffic jam ho toh thodi der wait karne ko kehta hai. Dono ko same treat karna galat hai.
how_it_works: `called = answers.some(a => a !== 'circuit-open')`; `if (!called) return out('circuit-open')`. Notifier: `if (result === 'circuit-open') { if (mode === 'first') failover; else retryLater(reopenInMs) }`.
in_this_project: `src/planner.ts::sendToAddresses` ka `if (!called) return out("circuit-open");`. `src/queued-notifier.ts` mein `BrokenCircuitError` par `reopenInMs = Math.max(reopenInMs, error.retryAfterMs); return "circuit-open";` aur circuit-open branch `stats.failedOver++`. README: "D6 (every device refused by an open circuit treated as an ordinary retryable failure, so an OTP waited instead of failing over to SMS -- no multi-device test opened the breaker)".
advantages: Dead channel par OTP turant fallback leta hai
Retry budget circuit refusals par waste nahi hota
Gap ab ek test se pinned hai
disadvantages: Mixed case (kuch circuit-open, kuch permanent) retryable hi rehta hai -- 'first' wahan wait karega
common_mistakes: Sirf single-device path test karke maan lena ki multi-device bhi chalega
Circuit-open ko generic retryable error banana
Breaker tests mein attempts aur fail-over dono check na karna
follow_up_questions: Why did the single-device tests not catch D6?
What does 'all' mode do in the same situation?
What other mixed cases would you add tests for?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: 'Down' (circuit open, koi call nahi) aur 'failed' (call hui, fail hui) alag signals hain; ek special value `"circuit-open"` unhe alag rakhti hai. Cost: CallResult type mein ek extra case jo har jagah handle karna padta hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Bina is rule ke: push provider down, breaker open, har OTP backoff ka wait -- login flow minutes tak atka. Mixed case: ek device circuit-open, ek permanent -> retryable; 'first' wahan retry karega, fail over nahi -- yeh conscious choice hai kyunki circuit wala device untried hai.
advanced.alternatives: Breaker per device nahi, per channel hai (provider-level health). Per-device breaker ka matlab nahi banta: device ka health provider ka health nahi.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bade scale par breaker shared state hona chahiye (har worker process ka apna breaker alag alag khulega); Redis jaisa shared counter ya provider status page integration.
advanced.production_improvements: Circuit open hone par alert, failedOver metric ka dashboard, aur breaker state per region -- yahan sab in-process hai.

question: Users report that working phones stopped getting push after a provider outage. How would you investigate, and how does gap D4 relate?
answer_hinglish:
Symptom: outage ke baad kuch users ko push aana band, jabki unke phones theek hain aur app installed hai. Yeh pattern "tokens galti se hata diye gaye" jaisa lagta hai.

Investigate: (1) user ka record dekho -- `users.get(id).pushTokens` khaali ya chhota hai? (2) Us user ki outage ke time ki notifications ka `GET /notifications/:id` -- push delivery ka `devices` log: kisi entry par `removed: true` ke saath `retryable: true` dikhe toh wahi bug. (3) Provider ke raw responses: outage mein 503 ke saath koi "invalid" flag bhi aa raha tha? (4) Agli notifications mein push `skipped (no_address)` -- yeh bhi confirm karta hai.

Cause, D4: rule hai ki token sirf tab hatega jab failure PERMANENT ho aur `invalidAddress: true` ho. D4 mutation ne `!a.retryable` check hata diya -- toh retryable failure (503) ke saath galat `invalidAddress` flag aaya toh bhi working token delete ho jaata. 503 device ke baare mein kuch nahi bolta, sirf provider ke baare mein. Survive isliye kiya kyunki kisi test ne yeh combination bheja hi nahi.

Fix: code mein condition `a.invalidAddress === true && !a.retryable` already hai; gap test se band hua -- 'invalidAddress on a RETRYABLE failure is ignored: the token stays'. Production lesson: destructive actions (data delete) ke liye strictest condition rakho aur us condition ke har hisse ka test likho. Users ko recover karne ke liye app agle start par token dobara register karti hai -- isliye register idempotent hai.
why_needed: Galat token removal silent data loss hai: koi error nahi, bas push aana band. Isliye destructive rule ki har shart ka test zaroori hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank ne server down hone par 'card invalid' maan kar tumhara card block kar diya. Server ki problem thi, card ki nahi.
how_it_works: `deviceLog` mein: answer failed hai, `invalidAddress === true` AND `retryable === false` -> `removePushToken` -> `entry.removed = true`.
in_this_project: `src/planner.ts::deviceLog` ki condition. `src/types.ts` ke `SendResult` mein `invalidAddress?: boolean` comment: FCM UNREGISTERED, APNs 410. README: "D4 (a dead-token removal on a RETRYABLE failure flagged invalid -- no test sent that combination)". Test `push.willAnswer({ status: "failed", retryable: true, reason: "503", invalidAddress: true })` ke baad `pushTokens` `["tok-a", "tok-b"]` hi rehte hain.
advantages: Removal sirf do sharton par: permanent + invalid
Device log mein `removed` flag se audit trail
Re-register idempotent, recovery aasaan
disadvantages: Provider ke galat flags par hum nirbhar hain
Hataya hua token wapas tabhi aata hai jab app register kare
common_mistakes: Sirf `invalidAddress` dekh kar delete karna
Delete ke rule ka sirf happy path test karna
Outage ke dauraan aaye errors ko device-level fact maan lena
follow_up_questions: Which provider responses map to invalidAddress in FCM and APNs?
How would you make token removal reversible or auditable?
Why did the mutation survive the first run?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Strict rule (do sharten) kabhi kabhi ek sach mein dead token ko ek round zyada rehne deta hai -- sasta cost. Loose rule working devices ko chup chaap kaat deta hai -- mehenga cost. Destructive side par strict hona sahi trade-off hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Provider bug ya adapter bug jo 5xx ko invalid map kare; mass removal ek outage mein hazaron users ka push band kar sakta hai. Defense: rule + test + metric (removals per minute).
advanced.alternatives: Soft delete (token ko 'suspect' mark karo, N baar invalid aane par hatao) ya removal ke baad grace period -- yahan built nahi, yahan ek hi permanent+invalid answer kaafi hai.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bade scale par removals ka rate monitor karo: normal din mein uninstall ke hisaab se steady, outage mein spike = bug ka signal.
advanced.production_improvements: Removal events ko log / audit table mein likhna, removals per provider ka alert, aur provider adapter mein response-code-to-flag mapping ke apne tests.

question: How does InMemoryUsers enforce the cap of 10 tokens per user, and what happens when a token is registered again?
answer_hinglish:
`addPushToken(userId, token)` teen kaam karta hai: pehle `checkPushToken(token)` (non-empty string, koi whitespace nahi, max 4096 chars, warna `INVALID_REQUEST`), phir user dhundta hai (nahi mila toh `false`), phir list update: same token pehle se hai toh use hata ke END par daal do, aur `slice(-MAX_PUSH_TOKENS)` se sirf aakhri 10 rakho.

Isse do rules ek saath milte hain. Re-register token ko NEWEST jagah le jaata hai -- matlab "yeh device zinda hai". Aur cap par OLDEST drop hota hai. Kyunki users app reinstall karte hain aur phone badalte hain bina unregister kiye, stale tokens jama hote rehte. Cap ke saath list bounded rehti hai, aur active devices (jo app khulne par baar baar register karte hain) hamesha list ke end par rehte hain, toh drop hone waale aksar wahi purane stale hote hain. Jo stale token phir bhi bach jaaye, woh pehli baar provider ke "dead" bolne par hat jaata hai.

`upsert` mein bhi check hai: 10 se zyada unique tokens wali list refuse. Aur `copy()` list ki copy deta hai -- test proof: `users.get("u1")!.pushTokens!.push("sneaky")` ke baad stored list `["t2"]` hi rehti hai.
why_needed: Bina cap ke har reinstall ek naya token jodta, list badhti rehti, aur har push un sab stale tokens ko call karta.
real_world_analogy: Phone ki 'recent calls' list: naya number upar aata hai, purana neeche se gir jaata hai, aur jisse dobara baat hui woh phir upar aa jaata hai.
how_it_works: filter (purana copy hatao) -> push (end par daalo) -> slice(-10) (sirf newest 10).
in_this_project: `src/users.ts`: `MAX_PUSH_TOKENS = 10`, `MAX_TOKEN_LENGTH = 4096`, `checkPushToken`, `InMemoryUsers.addPushToken`. Test 'add moves a known token to the newest place; over the cap the oldest is dropped': t1 re-register -> `["t2", "t1"]`, phir t3..t12 add karne par t1 aur t2 dono gaye, last `t12`.
advantages: List hamesha bounded
Active devices naturally bachte hain
Re-register idempotent (204 dobara bhi)
disadvantages: 11 asli active devices wala user ek kho dega (rare)
Oldest = least recently REGISTERED, least recently USED nahi
common_mistakes: Duplicate token list mein do baar daal dena
Cap par naya token refuse karna (naya device kaam hi nahi karega)
Internal array ka reference bahar de dena
follow_up_questions: Why drop the oldest instead of refusing the new token?
What is the difference between least recently registered and least recently used here?
Why does get() return a copy of the list?

question: Why does the push-token API never return the token list, and what input checks protect it?
answer_hinglish:
Push token ek capability hai: jiske paas token aur provider credentials hain, woh us device par push bhej sakta hai. Hamara API service-to-service hai (ek API key), par agar `GET` user ke tokens lauta de toh ek leaked API key, ek galat log line ya ek debug endpoint se saare users ke device addresses nikal sakte hain. Isliye design: `POST /users/:id/push-tokens` aur `DELETE /users/:id/push-tokens/:token` dono 204 dete hain, body khaali -- list kabhi echo nahi hoti. Jo cheez API ko kabhi dikhaani nahi, woh leak bhi nahi hogi.

Input checks (`checkPushToken`): string ho, empty na ho, whitespace na ho, max 4096 chars. Max length memory abuse rokta hai (har user ke 10 tokens x 4096 bounded), whitespace check malformed / injected values rokta hai. Non-string body (`{ token: 7 }`, `{}`, `[]`) 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`. Unknown user 404 -- typo'd user id par token store nahi hota. Registry configure nahi hai toh routes 404.

Baaki security stage 3 HTTP layer se aati hai: Bearer API key, constant-time compare, body parse se pehle auth. Honest limitation: API end user ko authenticate nahi karta -- app ka backend check kare ki logged-in user hi `:userId` hai, warna ek user doosre ke account par apna device register kar ke uske OTP push le sakta hai. Yeh README mein inbox ke liye explicitly likha hai aur yahan bhi lagta hai.
why_needed: Device addresses sensitive hain; unhe minimum jagah dikhana aur input bound karna basic defense hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank tumhara card number receipt par poora nahi chhaapta -- sirf zaroori kaam hota hai, poora data bahar nahi aata.
how_it_works: Route -> auth -> JSON check -> `checkPushToken` -> registry `addPushToken` (false -> 404) -> 204 no body.
in_this_project: `src/http/app.ts` routes `app.post("/users/:userId/push-tokens")` aur `app.delete("/users/:userId/push-tokens/:token")`, option `pushTokens?: PushTokenRegistry`. `src/users.ts::checkPushToken`. Tests 'register (twice is fine), unregister, unregister again -> 404; the token list is not echoed' (`[add.status, await add.text()]` == `[204, ""]`) aur 'bad token -> 400; unknown user -> 404; no registry configured -> 404'.
advantages: Token list kabhi response mein nahi
Bounded input size
Unknown user par kuch store nahi hota
disadvantages: End-user auth nahi -- app backend ki zimmedari
Token plaintext memory mein (real system mein DB mein encrypted-at-rest hona chahiye)
common_mistakes: Debug ke liye GET tokens endpoint bana dena
Tokens ko logs mein poora print karna
Bina user check ke kisi bhi :userId par register allow karna
follow_up_questions: How would a malicious user abuse device registration without end-user auth?
Should tokens be stored encrypted?
Why 204 with no body instead of returning the updated list?

question: What is the in-app inbox here, and why is it a fourth channel instead of a separate feature?
answer_hinglish:
In-app inbox woh bell icon hai jisme count dikhta hai aur list khulti hai -- "aapka order ship ho gaya", "20% off sale". Is project mein yeh `in_app` naam ka chautha channel hai (`CHANNELS = ["email", "sms", "push", "in_app"]`), aur iska "provider" kisi ko call nahi karta: `InboxSender.send()` message ko `InMemoryInbox` mein store kar deta hai aur item id ko providerId ki tarah lauta deta hai.

Channel kyun, alag code path kyun nahi? Kyunki tab saari machinery free mil jaati hai: catalog mein type `channels: ["push", "email", "in_app"]` likho, template do, aur preferences (marketing mute), modes (all / first), retries, queue, idempotency -- sab bina badle lagte hain. Alag feature hota toh yeh sab dobara likhna padta.

Channel ke apne rules: address user id hai (`addressesFor` in_app ke liye `[recipient.userId]` deta hai), toh har user ka inbox hai aur yeh kabhi `no_address` nahi. Yeh kisi ko jagata nahi, toh quiet hours ise defer nahi karte (`WAKES_USER` sirf sms aur push). Template mein subject ho sakta hai jo item ka title banta hai, aur HTML-escape nahi hota (app text render karti hai). Test: quiet hours mein marketing push `deferred`, uska inbox copy `sent`.
why_needed: Inbox ek durable copy deta hai jo push miss hone par bhi app mein milti hai; aur channel banane se existing rules reuse hote hain.
real_world_analogy: Ghar ka letterbox vs doorbell: doorbell (push) tumhe jagata hai, letterbox (inbox) chup chaap rakh leta hai, tum jab chaaho dekh lo.
how_it_works: Worker in_app delivery ko baaki channels ki tarah process karta hai; sender ka `send` = `inbox.add(message.to, { key, notificationId, title, body })`.
in_this_project: `src/types.ts` mein `CHANNELS` aur `addressesFor`, `src/policy.ts::WAKES_USER` (`["sms", "push"]`), `src/inbox.ts::InboxSender`, `src/catalog.ts` mein "in_app may have one (the item's title); sms and push have no subject line". Test 'quiet hours defer the push but not the inbox (it wakes nobody); a muted inbox is opted_out'.
advantages: Catalog, preferences, retries, queue sab reuse
Strategy pattern ka seedha faayda: ek aur ChannelSender
Quiet hours mein bhi message app mein turant
disadvantages: Inbox write bhi queue se hokar jaata hai (thoda delay)
Real-time push of new items (WebSocket / SSE) built nahi -- app poll karti hai
common_mistakes: Inbox ko alag API bana ke preferences bypass kar dena
in_app ko quiet hours mein defer karna
Inbox body ko HTML-escape karna jabki app text render karti hai

question: Why does the inbox use cursor paging instead of page numbers?
answer_hinglish:
Inbox newest first dikhta hai. Page numbers (`?page=2&limit=20`) ka matlab hai "20 skip karo, agle 20 do" -- offset. Problem: user ne page 1 dekha, us beech 3 naye items aa gaye. Ab page 2 ke liye offset 20 se shuru hota hai, par list 3 se neeche khisak gayi hai, toh page 1 ke aakhri 3 items page 2 par DOBARA dikhte hain. Ulta delete hone par items skip bhi ho sakte hain.

Cursor ka matlab hai "us item se purane do jo tumhe last mila tha". Yahan cursor last item ka sequence number hai. Naye items ka seq bada hota hai, toh "isse chhote seq waale" set ko koi nayi arrival nahi badal sakti -- page 2 hamesha wahi se shuru hota hai jahan page 1 khatam hua.

Test 'items arriving between two pages do not shift the next page': 10 items, page 1 (limit 4) = i10..i7, phir 3 naye add, page 2 = `["i6", "i5", "i4", "i3"]` -- koi repeat nahi; aur fresh first page par naye `["i13", "i12", "i11"]` upar hain.

Bonus: database mein bhi cursor (keyset pagination, `WHERE seq < $cursor ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT n`) index par seedha jaata hai, jabki bada OFFSET saari skipped rows padhta hai.
why_needed: Live feed (inbox, timeline) mein data paging ke dauraan badalta hai; offset paging wahan repeat aur skip karti hai.
real_world_analogy: Kitaab mein bookmark (cursor) vs 'page 50 kholo' -- agar kisi ne beech mein pages jod diye toh page 50 par alag content hoga, bookmark wahi rahega.
how_it_works: Pehla page: `before = Infinity`. Response ka `nextCursor` = page ke aakhri (sabse purane) item ka encoded seq. Agla page: `seq < before` waale items, newest first.
in_this_project: `src/inbox.ts` header comment: "Paging while new items arrive. Newest first, so ?page=2 would shift down by every new arrival and show items twice". `InMemoryInbox.page(userId, { limit, cursor })`. HTTP: `GET /users/:id/inbox?limit=20&cursor=<nextCursor>` -> `{ items, nextCursor, unread }`, `nextCursor: null` matlab last page.
advantages: Nayi arrivals se page shift nahi hota
DB mein index-friendly (keyset)
Last page ka saaf signal (nextCursor null)
disadvantages: 'Page 7 par jump karo' possible nahi
Total pages ka count nahi milta
common_mistakes: Live feed par OFFSET paging
Cursor mein timestamp lena jab do items ka time same ho sakta hai
Last page ke baad ek khaali extra page dena
follow_up_questions: Why is the cursor a sequence number and not a timestamp?
How would the SQL for this page look?
What if an item is deleted between two pages?

question: How is the inbox cursor encoded and checked, why must it be canonical, and how does page() find the starting point?
answer_hinglish:
Cursor `encodeCursor(seq)` = base64url of `"v1.<seq>"`. Do reasons: OPAQUE hai, toh client ise number samajh kar khud nahi banata (kal humne cursor ko `v2.<seq>.<shard>` kiya toh client nahi tootenge -- `v1` prefix isi version ke liye hai); aur API ka contract "jo humne diya wahi wapas bhejo" ban jaata hai.

`decodeCursor` strict hai: base64url decode, regex `^v1\.(\d{1,15})$`, aur phir CANONICAL check -- `encodeCursor(Number(match[1])) !== cursor` toh `INVALID_CURSOR`. Canonical kyun? Kyunki ek hi value ke kai spellings ho sakte hain: `v1.05` (leading zero) bhi 5 hai, aur base64url decoder extra `=` padding ya trailing bits ignore kar deta hai. Agar sab accept karein toh "jo humne diya wahi" wala contract toot jaata hai, caching / logging mein ek cursor ke kai roop hote, aur ek mutation check ("cursor not canonical") yahi pakadta hai. Test 5 bad cursors try karta hai: `garbage`, `""`, `v1.x`, `v1.05`, aur `encodeCursor(2) + "="`.

Starting point: `box.items` seq ascending sorted hai (end par append, front se drop). `page()` binary search se pehla index dhundta hai jiska `seq >= before`, phir wahan se peeche `limit` items leta hai aur reverse karta hai (newest first). `nextCursor` sirf tab jab `start > 0` -- isliye exact fit par khaali extra page nahi (45 items, limit 45 -> `nextCursor: null`). Cost O(log n + limit).
why_needed: Opaque aur strict cursor API ko future changes ke liye free rakhta hai aur galat input ko jaldi pakadta hai.
real_world_analogy: Cinema ticket ka barcode: tum use padh nahi sakte, sirf dikha sakte ho; aur photocopy ya haath se banaya barcode gate par reject hota hai.
how_it_works: decode -> regex -> re-encode compare -> seq. Phir lower-bound binary search on `items[mid].seq < before`, `slice(start, end).reverse()`.
in_this_project: `src/inbox.ts::encodeCursor` / `src/inbox.ts::decodeCursor`, `InMemoryInbox.page` ka `while (lo < end)` loop. HTTP layer (`src/http/app.ts`) `cursor=a&cursor=b` (array) ko bhi `INVALID_CURSOR` deta hai. Mutation checks: 'cursor not canonical', 'the cursor item repeated on the next page', 'an empty extra page' -- sab caught.
advantages: Client cursor ka format nahi jaanta, server badal sakta hai
Ek value ka ek hi valid spelling
O(log n) seek
disadvantages: Cursor signed nahi hai -- client valid-looking cursor bana sakta hai (sirf apne inbox mein, toh harmless)
Version prefix ka migration plan abhi nahi
common_mistakes: Raw seq / id ko cursor bana dena
Decoder ki leniency par bharosa karna
Exact fit par khaali last page
follow_up_questions: Should the cursor be signed (HMAC)? When does that matter?
Why \d{1,15} and not any length?
How does the binary search behave when the cursor item was dropped by retention?

question: Why is the unread count a stored counter changed only on a real state change, and what is the SQL equivalent?
answer_hinglish:
Unread count har page load par chahiye (bell icon), toh use har baar items gin kar nikaalna (`COUNT(*) WHERE read_at IS NULL`) mehenga hai jab inbox bada ho. Isliye ek stored counter: `box.unread`, padhna O(1).

Stored counter ka khatra drift hai: counter aur asli data alag ho jaayein. Rule jo use sahi rakhta hai: counter SIRF tab badlo jab item ki state sach mein badli. `markRead` mein `if (entry.readAt !== undefined) return "already_read"` -- already read item par counter nahi ghatta. Isliye do tabs ek hi item ko read mark karein toh count ek hi baar ghatega. `add` idempotent hai (same key par existing item, counter nahi badhta). Retention drop par sirf unread item gire toh counter ghatta hai. `markAllRead` jitne items asli mein badle (`marked`) utna hi ghataata hai.

SQL mein yahi shape (code comment mein likha hai): `UPDATE inbox_items SET read_at = now() WHERE id = $1 AND user_id = $2 AND read_at IS NULL` -- aur counter tabhi decrement karo jab row count 1 ho, same transaction mein: `UPDATE inbox_counters SET unread = unread - 1 WHERE user_id = $2`. `read_at IS NULL` condition hi concurrency guard hai: do concurrent updates mein se sirf ek row badlega, doosre ka row count 0.

Proof: randomized test (2000 random adds, reads, read-alls, page walks, 3 users) har step ke baad counter ko scratch se gine items se compare karta hai. Mutations "already-read decremented again", "counter not raised or lowered" caught.
why_needed: Har page load par count chahiye; stored counter fast hai par tabhi sahi hai jab har change exactly ek baar count ho.
real_world_analogy: Dukaan ka cash register: har sale par ek baar entry. Agar ek hi sale do counter-staff do baar likh dein toh shaam ko hisaab nahi milega.
how_it_works: State transition (unread -> read) par hi `unread--`; no-op transitions par kuch nahi. Add par `unread++`, retention drop of unread par `unread--`.
in_this_project: `src/inbox.ts` header comment aur `InMemoryInbox.markRead`, `markAllRead` (`box.unread -= marked`), `add` (retention loop `if (old.readAt === undefined) box.unread--`). Tests 'markRead: once marked, again already_read (the count drops once)' aur 'randomized: after every operation the counter equals the unread items counted from scratch'.
advantages: O(1) count read
Concurrent marks ek hi baar count
Randomized recount se drift ka proof
disadvantages: Counter row hot ho sakta hai (har user ka ek row -- par user-level contention kam hoti hai)
Ek bug se drift; repair job ki zaroorat production mein
common_mistakes: `UPDATE ... SET read_at = now() WHERE id = $1` bina `read_at IS NULL` ke, phir hamesha decrement
Counter aur item update alag transactions mein
Counter ko kabhi recount se verify na karna
follow_up_questions: How would you repair a drifted counter in production?
Why not compute the count with an index on (user_id) WHERE read_at IS NULL?
What isolation level does the conditional UPDATE need?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Stored counter = denormalization: fast read, par write path par discipline. Alternative partial index `ON inbox_items (user_id) WHERE read_at IS NULL` ke saath COUNT bhi chhote inbox (200 cap) par sasta hai -- 200 ki retention ki wajah se recount option bhi realistic hai. Counter tab jeetta hai jab reads bahut zyada hon.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Item update ho gaya par counter update fail (alag transaction) -> drift. Dono ek transaction mein ya ek CTE statement mein. Retention delete job counter adjust karna bhool jaaye -> drift; isliye yahan retention aur counter ek hi `add` function mein hain.
advanced.alternatives: Redis counter (INCR / DECR) cache ke roop mein + DB source of truth; ya har read par COUNT with partial index; ya event-sourced count. Yahan in-memory counter hai, koi DB nahi.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 100x users par counter rows users ke saath scale karti hain (per-user row, contention nahi). Ek celebrity broadcast (lakhon users ko ek saath item) par write fan-out counter updates ka bulk hota hai -- batch updates.
advanced.production_improvements: Periodic reconciliation job (sample users ka recount vs counter, drift metric), counter ko item table ke same shard par rakhna, aur read-all ko ek statement mein karna.

question: Why does mark all read take the newest item the user saw instead of marking everything unread?
answer_hinglish:
Race socho: user ne inbox khola, 5 unread dikhe, "mark all read" dabaya. Request server tak pahunchne ke beech ek naya item aa gaya -- OTP ka in-app copy ya order update. Agar "mark all read" ka matlab "abhi jo bhi unread hai sab" hota, toh woh naya item bhi read ho jaata -- jo user ne kabhi dekha hi nahi. Count 0 dikhta aur message chhoot jaata.

Isliye API `POST /users/:id/inbox/read-all { "upTo": "<itemId>" }` leti hai -- woh newest item jo user ki screen par tha. `markAllRead` items ko seq order mein walk karta hai aur `entry.seq > last.seq` par ruk jaata hai: usse naye items unread rehte hain. Jo already read hain unhe chhua nahi jaata, aur `marked` sirf asli changes ginta hai, toh counter sahi ghatta hai.

Test 'markAllRead up to the item the user saw: a newer arrival stays unread': i2 pehle se read, i4 aaya "while clicking", `markAllRead("u1", "i3")` = 2 (i1 aur i3), unread 1, aur i4 par `readAt` nahi. `upTo` kisi doosre user ka item ho ya na ho toh `undefined` -> HTTP 404; `upTo` missing toh 400.

Trade-off: client ko item id bhejna padta hai (thoda zyada contract), aur agar `upTo` item retention se gir gaya toh 404 -- client fresh page le ke dobara bheje. Yeh "intent ko data mein capture karo" pattern hai: server ko woh batao jo user ne dekha, na ki woh jo request ke time hai.
why_needed: Concurrent arrivals ke saath 'all' ka matlab ambiguous hai; user ne jo dekha wahi mark hona chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Manager kehta hai 'mere desk par jo files hain sab sign ho gayi' -- par jo file abhi peon ne rakhi, woh usne dekhi bhi nahi; use sign maanna galat hai.
how_it_works: `last = box.byId.get(upTo)`; items oldest-first walk; `seq > last.seq` par break; unread par `readAt = now`, `marked++`; end mein `box.unread -= marked`.
in_this_project: `src/inbox.ts::markAllRead` ("Marks every unread item up to and including `upToItemId` (the newest one the user saw)"). `src/http/app.ts` read-all route: `upTo` string na ho toh 400 "upTo must be the id of the newest item the user saw", `undefined` -> 404. Mutation 'read-all marking newer items' aur '`upTo` unchecked' caught.
advantages: Unseen items kabhi galti se read nahi
Counter exact
Doosre user ke item id se kuch nahi hota
disadvantages: Client ko newest seen id track karna padta hai
upTo retention se gir jaaye toh 404, retry chahiye
Walk O(n) per call (n <= 200 yahan)
common_mistakes: Server time par 'sab' mark karna
upTo ka owner check na karna
Already read items ko bhi count kar ke counter ghataana
follow_up_questions: What should the client do if upTo returns 404?
How would this be one SQL statement?
Would a timestamp instead of an item id work? What breaks?

question: A job is redelivered after a worker dies, so the in_app message is sent twice. Why does the user still see one inbox item, and where can that guarantee break?
answer_hinglish:
Queue at-least-once hai: worker ne in_app send kiya (item store ho gaya), phir job complete karne se pehle mar gaya ya stall hua. Lease expire, doosra worker same job uthata hai aur `InboxSender.send` dobara chalata hai. Bina protection ke inbox mein do same items aur unread count 2.

Protection: `add()` provider idempotency key par keyed hai -- in_app ke liye woh `<notificationId>:in_app` hai, har attempt par same. `box.byKey.get(input.key)` mila toh existing item ka view lautao, kuch store nahi, counter nahi badhta. Sender same item id ko providerId deta hai, toh dono attempts ka result same hai. Test 'the same message sent twice (a redelivered job) is one inbox item': `b` equals `a`, unread 1. Mutations 'add not idempotent' aur 'a random storage key' dono caught.

Yeh wahi idea hai jo real providers ke saath hum chahte hain -- fark yeh ki yahan "provider" hum khud hain, toh dedupe ki guarantee hamare haath mein hai, sirf hope nahi.

Kahan toot sakta hai (honest): (1) `byKey` sirf un items ka hai jo abhi inbox mein hain. Retention (200) se item gir gaya aur phir ek bahut late redelivery aayi, toh naya item ban jaayega. (2) Process restart par sab in-memory hai -- inbox hi chala jaata hai. Real system mein `UNIQUE (user_id, idem_key)` constraint aur `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` yeh guarantee durable banata.
why_needed: At-least-once system mein har side effect idempotent hona chahiye, warna retries duplicates banate hain.
real_world_analogy: Register mein entry se pehle receipt number check karna: same receipt number dobara aaya toh nayi entry nahi.
how_it_works: `add`: `existing = box.byKey.get(key)` -> return view; warna naya entry, `byKey.set`, `unread++`, retention loop jo `byKey.delete(old.key)` bhi karta hai.
in_this_project: `src/inbox.ts::InMemoryInbox` ka `add` ("Idempotent on `key`: the same key again returns the item already stored (while it is still in the inbox)"). Key `src/planner.ts::outboundMessage` se: in_app ke liye `${record.id}:${delivery.channel}`.
advantages: Redelivery par ek hi item
Counter sahi rehta hai
Same providerId, toh receipts / logs consistent
disadvantages: Dedupe sirf retained items tak
In-memory: restart par sab gaya
common_mistakes: Har add par random key use karna
Idempotency sirf queue level par maan kar sender ko non-idempotent chhod dena
Dedupe key ko retention ke saath delete karke sochna ki forever dedupe hai
follow_up_questions: How long must the dedupe key live compared to the queue's redelivery window?
How would ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING return the existing item id?
What other side effects in this system need the same treatment?

question: How does the inbox prevent one user from reading or marking another user's items, and who is responsible for authenticating the end user?
answer_hinglish:
Do layers hain aur dono ki zimmedari alag hai.

Layer 1, jo yahan built hai: har lookup ek user ke inbox ke ANDAR hota hai. `markRead(userId, itemId)` pehle `this.boxes.get(userId)` leta hai, phir usi box ke `byId` mein item dhundta hai. Agar itemId kisi doosre user ka hai, toh woh is box mein hai hi nahi -> `not_found` -> HTTP 404. Koi global `items.get(itemId)` nahi hai jisse id guess karke (IDOR -- insecure direct object reference) doosre ka item chhua jaa sake. `markAllRead` mein `upTo` bhi usi box mein dhunda jaata hai. Test: u2 ka item i4 -- `markRead("u1", "i4")` `not_found` aur u2 ka count 1 hi. Mutation 'lookups across users' caught. 404 (403 nahi) bhi soch kar: item exist karta hai ya nahi, yeh bhi leak nahi hota.

Layer 2, jo yahan NAHI hai: API ek service API key se authenticate karta hai -- woh batata hai "yeh hamara backend hai", yeh nahi ki "yeh user u1 hai". Toh agar app ka backend kisi logged-in user u2 ki request par bina check kiye `/users/u1/inbox` call kar de, toh u1 ka inbox u2 ko dikh jaayega. README aur `src/http/app.ts` comment saaf likhte hain: app ka backend check kare ki logged-in user hi `:userId` hai.

Production mein: end-user token (JWT / session) app backend verify kare, ya inbox API khud per-user tokens accept kare (`sub` claim == `:userId`), aur service keys ke scopes ho (`inbox:read`).
why_needed: Multi-tenant data mein 'id pata hai toh access hai' sabse common security bug hai; scoping aur authentication dono chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Hotel ka room key card sirf tumhare room ka darwaza kholta hai, chahe tumhe doosre room ka number pata ho. Par reception (app backend) ko pehle check karna hai ki card sahi guest ko diya.
how_it_works: Har method ka pehla step `boxes.get(userId)`; item id sirf us box ke Maps mein resolve hota hai. HTTP route `requireUser(:userId)` unknown user par 404.
in_this_project: `src/inbox.ts` comment: "Items are looked up inside one user's inbox only, so user A cannot mark user B's item read by guessing its id". `src/http/app.ts` option comment: "The caller (the app's backend) must check that the logged-in ...". Tests: 'markRead ... another user's item is not_found', HTTP 'another user's item -> 404', read-all with u2's item -> 404.
advantages: Id guess karke cross-user access impossible
404 existence leak nahi karta
Limitation documented, chhupi nahi
disadvantages: End-user auth app backend par chhoda gaya
Ek service key sab users ka inbox padh sakti hai (no scopes)
common_mistakes: Global item lookup by id phir owner check bhoolna
Service API key ko user identity samajhna
Cross-user par 403 dena (existence leak)
follow_up_questions: How would you add per-user tokens to this API?
Why 404 and not 403 for another user's item?
How would scopes on service keys look?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Scoping data-layer par (har query mein user_id) defense in depth hai -- auth layer mein bug ho toh bhi galat id se data nahi milta. Par scoping authentication ka replacement nahi: kaun user hai yeh kisi ko verify karna hi padega.
advanced.failure_scenarios: App backend bina check ke `:userId` forward kare -> horizontal privilege escalation. Service API key leak -> saare inboxes readable. Dono README-documented risks hain.
advanced.alternatives: Inbox API ko seedha mobile app se call karwana per-user JWT ke saath (`sub` == userId), ya API gateway jo user claim inject kare. Row-level security (Postgres RLS) DB par bhi.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Scale se rule nahi badalta, par sharding by user_id ke saath scoping natural ho jaati hai: query hamesha ek shard ke ek user tak.
advanced.production_improvements: Per-caller keys aur scopes, end-user token verification, cross-user 404 ka metric (enumeration attempt ka signal), audit log for read-all.

question: Add markUnread(userId, itemId) to InMemoryInbox so the stored unread counter stays correct, and write the tests that prove it.
answer_hinglish:
Rule wahi rakhna hai jo baaki inbox ka hai: counter sirf asli state change par badle, aur lookup sirf us user ke box ke andar ho.

Implementation: box aur entry `this.boxes.get(userId)?.byId.get(itemId)` se lo -- nahi mila toh `not_found` (doosre user ka item bhi yahi). Item already unread hai (`readAt === undefined`) toh `already_unread` aur kuch nahi badlo -- yeh do tabs ke concurrent "mark unread" ko ek hi baar count karwata hai. Warna `delete entry.readAt` aur `box.unread++`, return `marked`.

Tests teen: (1) read item ko unread karo -> count +1, dobara karo -> `already_unread`, count same; (2) doosre user ka item -> `not_found`, dono counts same; (3) sabse important -- existing randomized test mein ek branch jodo jo random `markUnread` bhi kare. Woh test har step ke baad counter ko scratch se recount karta hai, toh koi bhi galti (double increment, retention ke saath interaction) turant pakdi jaayegi. Seed ka sequence badlega -- yeh naya test case hai, purane seeds ke scenarios ko nahi chhedna, isliye naya `it(...)` likho, purane loop ki probabilities mat badlo (NTF-100 wala lesson).

HTTP: `POST /users/:userId/inbox/:itemId/unread` -> 204, `not_found` par 404, bilkul read route ki tarah. Mutation sochke dekho: `if (entry.readAt === undefined)` check hatao -> test (1) fail hona chahiye.
why_needed: Naya state transition jodna sabse common change hai, aur stored counter wale design mein yahi jagah drift laati hai.
real_world_analogy: Email mein 'mark as unread' -- agar har click par counter badhe chahe mail pehle se unread ho, toh badge galat number dikhayega.
how_it_works: Lookup scoped -> no-op check -> state change + counter change, ek saath.
in_this_project: Pattern `src/inbox.ts::markRead` se copy hota hai (`MarkResult`, `boxes.get(userId)?.byId.get(itemId)`). Tests `test/inbox.test.ts` ke `inboxWith(n)` helper aur randomized counter test ke style mein. Yeh method repo mein NAHI hai -- exercise hai.
advantages: Counter discipline same rule se
User scoping reuse
Randomized recount naye transition ko bhi cover karta hai
disadvantages: Ek aur state transition = ek aur jagah drift ka risk
markAllRead ka 'up to' contract markUnread ke saath interact karta hai (user ne unread kiya item read-all se phir read ho sakta hai)
common_mistakes: Hamesha `unread++` karna
Global lookup by item id
Purane randomized test ki probabilities badal kar seeds ke scenarios bigaadna
follow_up_questions: Should read-all re-mark an item the user explicitly marked unread?
What mutation would you run against markUnread?
How does the SQL version of markUnread look?

question: Write a test proving that a worker which lost its lease still removes a dead token, but does not write its device log over the new owner's.
answer_hinglish:
Test ko teen cheezein dikhani hain: (1) stalled worker ka provider answer lease expire hone ke BAAD aaye; (2) beech mein naya owner delivery bhej de; (3) stalled worker ke `invalidAddress` answer se token user se hat jaaye, par delivery ka `devices` log naye owner ka hi rahe.

Setup `test/devices.test.ts` ke existing stalled-worker test jaisa: user ke do tokens, `setupQueued` (leaseMs 30 000). Do `gate()` promises se pehle worker ki dono calls hawa mein latki rehti hain. `notifier.claim(4)` + `notifier.process(j)` manually chalao (yahi stalled worker hai), `clock.advance(30_000)` se lease khatam, phir `worker.drain()` naya owner. Naye owner ke liye script: tok-a par `failed(true, "503")`, tok-b default sent -> delivery sent, log `tok-a:failed, tok-b:sent`.

Ab stalled worker ke gates resolve karo: tok-a ko `dead` (permanent + invalidAddress), tok-b ko late retryable. `deviceLog` lease check se PEHLE chalta hai, toh tok-a `removePushToken` se hat jaata hai. Phir lease check fail -> `lostLease()`, log assign nahi.

Asserts: user ke tokens `["tok-b"]`; delivery `sent`, uska log naye owner wala (`tok-a` par `removed` flag NAHI, kyunki woh stalled worker ka tha); `stats.leaseLost >= 1`. Mutation check: lease check ko `devices` assignment ke neeche le jao -> log assert fail; removal ko lease check ke peeche le jao -> tokens assert fail. Dono direction pin ho gayi.
why_needed: Asymmetric rule (ek write fenced, ek nahi) ko sirf ek test hi dono taraf se pin kar sakta hai; warna koi refactor chupke se ek side badal dega.
real_world_analogy: Do guards ki shift change ka drill: purana guard late report deta hai -- 'taala toota' wali baat maani jaati hai, par uski register entry naye guard ki entry ke upar nahi likhi jaati.
how_it_works: Manual claim + process = controlled stalled worker; ManualClock se lease expiry; gates se provider answers ka timing control.
in_this_project: Helpers: `test/queued-helpers.ts::setupQueued` (leaseMs 30_000, retry maxAttempts 3), `failed()`, `orderReq()`; `test/helpers.ts::gate`, `FULL_USER`. Existing test 'a worker that lost its lease does not write its device log over the new owner's' sirf log side check karta hai; yeh exercise removal side bhi jodta hai. Yeh exact test repo mein nahi hai.
advantages: Asymmetry dono taraf se pinned
Real timers ke bina deterministic (ManualClock + gates)
Existing helpers reuse
disadvantages: Test provider call order par nirbhar (FakeSender script FIFO)
Email job bhi stall hota hai -- assert sirf push delivery par
common_mistakes: Sirf ek side assert karna
Real setTimeout / sleep se lease expiry karna (flaky)
Gates resolve karne se pehle `await stalled` (deadlock)
follow_up_questions: Which mutation would each assert catch?
Why does the email job of the same notification not break this test?
How would you write the same test against a real queue like SQS?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Manual `claim` + `process` test ko worker loop se bypass karta hai -- zyada control, par test internal API par depend karta hai. Trade-off accept hai kyunki lease race ko real timers se reproduce karna flaky hota.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar kal koi `sendToAddresses` ko refactor karke removal ko caller mein (lease check ke baad) le jaaye, toh tokens assert fail. Agar log assignment lease check se upar chala jaaye, toh log assert fail.
advanced.alternatives: Property-based / randomized test (queued-invariants mein dying workers already hain) par wahan yeh specific asymmetry assert nahi hoti; targeted test zyada clear hai.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Scale se test nahi badalta; par production mein yahi scenario lambi provider latency par baar baar hoga, isliye leaseLost metric zaroori.
advanced.production_improvements: Is test ko mutation runner ki list mein jodna (dono mutations), aur same pattern receipts ke parked-apply path par bhi.

question: How do the seeded randomized invariant tests work, and why were they pinned to their 3 channels when in_app was added?
answer_hinglish:
Randomized invariant test ek chhota simulator hai. `prng(seed)` ek deterministic random generator hai; usse hazaron random scenarios bante hain -- users (kuch ke paas phone, kuch ke paas token), random mutes aur quiet windows, offsets, provider ke random answers, client retries, aur queued version mein workers jo job pakde pakde mar jaate hain. Har provider call par test rules ko KHUD, independently (Date arithmetic se, `policy.ts` se nahi) dobara calculate karta hai aur check karta hai. End mein invariants: har record finished, `first` ne max ek channel bheja, attempts <= 3, har sent delivery ek hi baar. Stage 1: 8 seeds x 300 requests; stage 2: 6 seeds x 250 requests, 3 workers.

Seed kyun? Failure reproducible ho. Seed 5 ne asli bug pakda tha -- hourly flush quiet window ka 15-minute gap miss kar deta tha, aur late flush ne agli raat ki quiet hours mein marketing push bhej diya tha (fix: send time par replan).

Pinning: preferences pehle `CHANNELS.filter(() => rand() < 0.3)` se bante the. `in_app` jodne par CHANNELS mein 4 items ho gaye, matlab har user par EK EXTRA `rand()` call. PRNG ka poora sequence shift ho jaata -- har seed ka har scenario badal jaata, aur woh seeds jo kabhi bug-finding scenarios dete the, ab kuch aur test karte. Isliye list explicitly `["email", "sms", "push"]` kar di gayi: same random stream, same scenarios. Inbox ka apna alag randomized test hai (seed 7, 2000 operations).

Debugging lesson: randomized test mein koi bhi change jo `rand()` calls ki ginti badle, woh chupke se test ko badal deta hai.
why_needed: Randomized tests woh combinations dhundhte hain jo haath se likhe tests nahi sochte; seed unhe reproducible banata hai, aur stable stream unhe regression guard.
real_world_analogy: Ek recorded cricket match ka replay: same recording, same balls. Agar beech mein ek extra ball daal do toh baaki saari balls ka order badal jaata hai aur woh famous wicket kabhi nahi aata.
how_it_works: `prng(seed)` -> scenario generation -> har send par independent rule check -> end invariants. Same seed = same `rand()` sequence = same scenario, jab tak calls ki ginti same rahe.
in_this_project: `test/invariants.test.ts` (`for (const seed of [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8])`, comment mein seed 5 ka zikr) aur `test/queued-invariants.test.ts` (`[11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16]`). Commit 4206709: "randomized tests pinned to their 3 channels so the seeds keep their scenarios" -- `mutedMarketing: (["email", "sms", "push"] as Channel[]).filter(() => rand() < 0.3)`. Inbox: `test/inbox.test.ts` randomized counter test.
advantages: Hazaron combinations sasta
Failure seed se reproducible
Pinning se purane bug-finding scenarios bache
disadvantages: Naya channel (in_app) in randomized runs mein cover nahi hota -- alag tests par nirbhar
Seed-dependent tests brittle: random calls ki ginti badli toh scenarios badle
common_mistakes: Math.random() use karna (reproduce nahi hoga)
Rules ko test mein policy.ts se hi calculate karna (same bug dono jagah)
Generator code badal kar sochna ki test 'wahi' hai
follow_up_questions: How would you extend the randomized tests to cover in_app without shifting the old seeds?
Why compute the expected rules independently of policy.ts?
How do you choose how many seeds and requests to run?

question: What are mutation checks, why were they used as the measure of test quality here, and what did the survivors teach?
answer_hinglish:
Mutation check: code mein jaan boojh kar ek chhota bug daalo (ek condition hatao, `>=` ko `>` karo, ek line skip karo), poora suite chalao, aur dekho koi test fail hota hai ya nahi. Fail hua = mutation "caught"; nahi hua = "survived", matlab tests us behaviour ko dekh hi nahi rahe. Har mutation akela apply hota hai, phir file byte-for-byte restore. Coverage sirf batata hai line chali; mutation batata hai line ka RESULT kisi ne check kiya.

Numbers (README): stage 1 43, stage 2 77 (43 moved + 34 new), HTTP API 25, receipts 24, devices 21, inbox 20 -- sab caught, documented survivors close karne ke baad. Total 192 tests.

Survivors ne kya sikhaya -- har ek ek test gap tha: Q5 (pre-1970 modulo; test 23:00 par tha jahan galat arithmetic bhi sahi answer deta hai), C2 (test ka type doosri wajah se bhi invalid tha), S22 (cap store fail hone ke baad lease check -- stalled worker ne SENT par pending likh diya), S24, W2 (start() twice -- purana test doosra loop dekh hi nahi sakta tha), H15 (unknown user ke liye PUT), D4 aur D6 (multi-device ke untested combinations). Pattern: survivors wahan the jahan test "kuch aur" ki wajah se pass ho raha tha, ya ek combination kabhi bheja hi nahi gaya.

Ek aur lesson: kuch tests mutation run se PEHLE tighten kiye gaye (receipts merge test "last one wins" se bhi pass hota; inbox ke liye `limit=1e1` test), kyunki test ka sawal yeh hai "kya yeh galat implementation ko reject karta hai?". Aur J6 / S6 hang se caught hue (runner 180 s baad rokta hai).
why_needed: Tests ki quality ka seedha measure chahiye; 'sab green hai' yeh nahi batata ki tests bugs pakdenge.
real_world_analogy: Fire drill: building mein jaan boojh kar nakli aag ka alarm -- dekhna ki sprinklers aur log sach mein react karte hain ya sirf poster lage hain.
how_it_works: Mutation list -> ek apply -> `npm test` -> caught / survived -> restore -> agla. Survivor = naya test likho, phir dobara chalao.
in_this_project: README sections 'Mutation checks', 'Stage 2: mutation checks', 'Stage 3: HTTP API', 'Stage 3: delivery receipts', 'Stage 3: several push devices', 'Stage 3: the in-app inbox' mein har area ki list (P1..P4, Q1..Q8, S1..S25, J1..J6, W1..W3, D4, D6, H15). Tests jo survivors ne bulwaaye: devices.test.ts ke 'invalidAddress on a RETRYABLE failure is ignored' aur 'every device's call refused by an open circuit'.
advantages: Test gaps ka seedha signal
Survivor list = concrete todo
Refactor ke baad confidence (stage 2 ne stage 1 ke 43 dobara chalaye)
disadvantages: Haath se chuni mutations -- jo nahi sochi, woh check nahi hui
Slow: har mutation par poora suite
Equivalent mutants (jo behaviour nahi badalte) time lete hain
common_mistakes: Coverage ko test quality samajhna
Survivor ko 'harmless' bol kar ignore karna
Mutation ke baad file restore na karna
follow_up_questions: How would you automate this with a tool like Stryker, and what would you lose?
What is an equivalent mutant?
Why did J6 count as caught by a hang?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Hand-picked mutations targeted hain (har design rule ke liye ek), par incomplete. Stryker jaisa tool hazaron mutants generate karta hai -- zyada coverage, zyada noise aur time. Yahan conscious choice: rule-based list, documented.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Tooling khud fail ho sakta hai: mutation runner ka timeout branch pehle `taskkill /IM node.exe` chalata tha (machine ke saare Node processes maar deta) aur forever-loop wale mutant (J6) par pipe read ghanton atka -- ab sirf apna process tree kill karta hai. Lesson: test infrastructure bhi code hai, uske bhi failure modes hain.
advanced.alternatives: Property-based testing (fast-check) invariants ke liye; coverage gates; manual review checklists. Mutation testing in sab ko complement karta hai, replace nahi.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x codebase par har mutation ke liye poora suite mehenga; production teams sirf changed files par incremental mutation testing CI mein chalati hain.
advanced.production_improvements: CI mein incremental mutation run, survivors ko PR comment mein dikhana, aur har naye feature ke saath uski mutation list README mein likhna (jaise yahan har stage ki hai).

question: If you moved this system to a relational database, what schema would you use for records, deliveries, push tokens and the inbox?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle honesty: is project mein koi database nahi hai -- sab in memory hai. Yeh design hai jo main production ke liye propose karunga, code ke shapes se nikla hua.

Tables:
- `notifications (id PK, user_id, type_id, category, mode, idempotency_key, request_fingerprint, created_at)` + `UNIQUE (user_id? / caller, idempotency_key)` jo 24 h ke baad purge ho (Stripe jaisa).
- `deliveries (notification_id, channel, status, to_address, body, subject, attempts, not_before, next_attempt_at, skip_reason, provider_id, error, retryable, receipt_event, receipt_at, lease_token, PRIMARY KEY (notification_id, channel))` -- ek channel ek delivery, jaise code mein. Index `(channel, provider_id)` receipts ke lookup ke liye (code ka `sentBy` map).
- `delivery_devices (notification_id, token, status, provider_id, error, retryable, removed, PK (notification_id, token))` -- per-device log, JSON column bhi chal sakta hai kyunki yeh sirf last answer hai.
- `push_tokens (user_id, token, registered_at, PK (user_id, token))` -- cap 10 ek trigger / app logic se: insert ke baad `registered_at` ke hisaab se oldest delete. Re-register = `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET registered_at = now()`.
- `inbox_items (user_id, seq BIGSERIAL, id UUID UNIQUE, idem_key, notification_id, title, body, created_at, read_at, PK (user_id, seq), UNIQUE (user_id, idem_key))` + `inbox_counters (user_id PK, unread)`.
- Jobs: `jobs (id, run_at, priority, lease_until, lease_token, payload)` claimed with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` -- ya ek broker.

Key decisions: sab `user_id` se lead karte hain taaki sharding by user natural ho; inbox page query `WHERE user_id = $1 AND seq < $2 ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT $3` PK index par; retention 200 ek periodic delete ya insert ke saath.
why_needed: In-memory design ko durable banana interview ka standard follow-up hai; schema batata hai ki kaunse invariants DB constraints se milenge.
real_world_analogy: Rough notebook ka hisaab (in memory) vs bank ka ledger (DB) -- ledger mein har column ka matlab fix hai aur galat entry constraint rokta hai.
how_it_works: Har in-memory Map ek table / index ban jaata hai: `byKey` -> UNIQUE (user_id, idem_key), `byId` -> UNIQUE id, `items` sorted by seq -> PK (user_id, seq), `sentBy` -> index (channel, provider_id).
